references.text: Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt, illustrating the consequences of disobeying God's instruction not to look back.
Jeremiah's exhortation 'Flee, save your life!' is a direct parallel to the angel's command to Lot: 'Flee for your life' (הִמָּלֵט עַל־נַפְשֶׁךָ).
Jesus refers to Lot's wife as an example of the consequences of looking back or longing for one's former life when called to follow God.
Jesus' words that no one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God reflect the principle of not looking back given to Lot.
Jesus' instructions to flee without hesitation or turning back during the great tribulation recall the commands given to Lot at the destruction of Sodom.
A direct linguistic and theological parallel: a warning to separate from the ungodly to avoid being 'swept away' in God's judgment.
A clear thematic parallel: a divine command not to turn back, where obedience is crucial for life or integrity.
